Vedic Calendar & Seasonal Traditions

South Indian Sacred Festivals

From Varamahalakshmi and Ganesha Habba to Ugadi, Vishu, and Thai Pongal — discover authentic regional rituals, required samagri manifests, and consecrated festival kits.

Region:
Season:
Shravana (July – August)Friday

श्री वरलक्ष्मी व्रतम्

Sri Varalakshmi Vrata (Varamahalakshmi)

Observed by married women (Sumangalis) across South India on the Friday preceding the Shravana full moon. The Kalasha is crowned with a silver or brass Lakshmi face, draped in red silk, and honored with the tying of the sacred nine-knot yellow cotton thread (Nombu Saradu / Thorana).

Karnataka Practice:Silver or brass Lakshmi Mukhavada installation • Chigali and Thambittu sweet offerings

Bhadrapada (August – September)Monday

श्री गणेश चतुर्थी

Ganesh Chaturthi (Ganesha Habba / Vinayaka Chavithi)

The premier community and family observance celebrating the birth of Lord Ganesha on Bhadrapada Shukla Chavithi. Families install unbaked clay idols (Matti Ganapati), invoke his presence with 21 sacred leaves (Eka Vimshathi Patri), and offer Modaka and Kadubu sweets.

Karnataka Practice:Pure clay Clay Ganapati (Bommbe) • Fried Modaka and steamed Karigadubu
karnatakatamil naduandhra pradeshtelanganakerala

Bhadrapada (Day before Ganesha Chaturthi)Sunday

स्वर्ण गौरी व्रतम्

Gowri Habba (Swarna Gowri Vrata)

Celebrated the day before Ganesh Chaturthi across Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh. Married daughters return to their maternal homes as Goddess Gowri is invoked in a conical turmeric form (Arishina Gowri), accompanied by the exchange of traditional bamboo Bagina winnowing trays.

Karnataka Practice:Twin bamboo winnowing trays (Mora) lined with Arishina-Kunkuma • 16 traditional sacred items (dals, rice, jaggery, bangle pair, mirror, comb)
karnatakaandhra pradeshtelangana

श्री कृष्ण जन्माष्टमी

Krishna Janmashtami (Gokulashtami / Sri Krishna Jayanthi)

Celebrates the divine midnight avatar of Lord Krishna during the Rohini Nakshatra. South Indian households draw miniature baby footprints with rice flour paste leading from the entrance threshold to the mandir, symbolizing Krishna walking into the home.

Tamil Nadu Practice:Rice flour baby Krishna footprints (Kutty Kaal kolam) • Seedai (Uppu Seedai and Vella Seedai)

Ashwina (September – October)October 11 – 20

शारदीय नवरात्रि एवं विजयादशमी

Navaratri & Dasara (Ayudha Puja & Saraswati Puja)

A ten-day celebration culminating in Vijayadashami. In Tamil Nadu, families arrange thematic doll stairs (Bommai Golu); in Karnataka, Mysore Dasara honors Chamundeshwari; on Maha Navami, vehicles, tools, and professional instruments receive sacred Ayudha Puja.

Karnataka Practice:Ayudha Puja: Sanctifying vehicles, cutting tools, and books with Kumkum, Turmeric & Ash gourd (Boodu Kumbalakai) • Chamundeshwari Archana with pure Bilva and red hibiscus
karnatakatamil naduandhra pradeshtelanganakerala

Ashwina / Kartika (October – November)November 8 – 10

दीपावली एवं नरक चतुर्दशी

Deepavali (Naraka Chaturdashi & Lakshmi Deeparadhana)

Celebrated with distinct Vedic custom in South India: the day begins before sunrise on Naraka Chaturdashi with the sacred Gingelly (Sesame) Oil Bath with warm water representing Ganga Snanam, consuming herbal Deepavali Legiyam, and lighting rows of clay and brass deepams.

Tamil Nadu Practice:Auspicious Sesame Oil smeared by elders before dawn • "Ganga Snanam Aacha?" morning greeting
tamil nadukarnatakaandhra pradeshtelanganakerala

Chaitra (March – April)Tuesday

युगादि

Ugadi / Yugadi (Telugu & Kannada New Year)

Marks the commencement of the new Vedic Luni-Solar calendar (Pratipada of Chaitra masa). Households tie mango leaf toranams, read the yearly Panchanga predictions (Panchanga Sravanam), and consume the signature Bevu-Bella / Ugadi Pachadi combining six tastes.

Karnataka Practice:Bevu (bitter neem flowers) mixed with Bella (sweet jaggery) • Kayiholige / Bele Holige (sweet stuffed flatbread)
karnatakaandhra pradeshtelangana

Medam (Mid April)Wednesday

विषु

Vishu (Malayalam Sacred New Dawn)

The astrological New Year of Kerala, marking the sun’s entry into Medam rasi. The night before, elders arrange the sacred Vishukkani in a bronze Uruli with golden cucumbers, Kani Konna flowers, raw rice, mirror, and Nilavilakku. Family members open their eyes first to this sacred vision at dawn.

Kerala Practice:Bronze Uruli containing Kani Vellarikka (golden cucumber), raw rice, and gold coins • Kani Konna (Cassia fistula) bright yellow blossom bunches

Thai / Makara (January)Thursday

मकर संक्रान्ति एवं पोंगल

Pongal / Makara Sankranti

The solar transit into Makara rasi (Uttarayana). In Tamil Nadu, Thai Pongal is observed by boiling freshly harvested rice and jaggery in an earthen or brass pot tied with fresh turmeric leaves until it boils over with joyous cries of "Pongalo Pongal!". In Karnataka and AP, Ellu-Bella is shared.

Tamil Nadu Practice:Consecrated Pongal pot tied with raw turmeric and ginger shoots • Sweet Sakkarai Pongal cooked in outdoor courtyard facing morning sun
tamil nadukarnatakaandhra pradeshtelangana

Chithirai (Mid April)Wednesday

पुத்தாண்டு (वर्ष पिरप्पु)

Tamil New Year (Puthandu / Varusha Pirappu)

Celebrated on the first day of the Tamil month Chithirai. On new year morning, families view the auspicious Kanni tray containing betel leaves, fruits, gold jewellery, flowers, and a mirror before welcoming elders with prostrations.

Tamil Nadu Practice:Kanni darshanam arranged with seasonal fruits (Mango, Jackfruit, Banana — Mukkani) • Maanga Pachadi combining raw mango, jaggery, red chillies, and bitter neem flowers
tamil nadu
